questions.prompt: Name a ritual of Hajj or Umrah.

answers.explanation: Walking seven times around the Ka'bah.
The sacred state pilgrims enter, with men wearing two plain white sheets.

source.text: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Hajj; Sahih Muslim, Book of Hajj

answers.explanation: Walking seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwah, as Hajar did searching for water.
The heart of Hajj: standing in prayer at Arafah on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah. "Hajj is Arafah."
Throwing pebbles at the three pillars in Mina, recalling Ibrahim's rejection of Shaytan.

source.text: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Hajj; Sahih Muslim, Book of Hajj

answers.explanation: Offering an animal (the hady) and sharing its meat.
Men shave or shorten their hair (women trim a little) to leave ihram.
Spending the night under the open sky at Muzdalifah after Arafah.
Calling out "Labbayk Allahumma labbayk" — "Here I am, O Allah, here I am."
Staying in the tent city of Mina during the days of Hajj.

source.text: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Hajj; Sahih Muslim, Book of Hajj

answers.explanation: The essential tawaf of Hajj, made after Arafah.
Drinking from the blessed well of Zamzam.
Kissing, touching or pointing to the Black Stone at each circuit.
Two units of prayer behind the Station of Ibrahim after tawaf.
The last tawaf before leaving Makkah.
The tawaf of arrival on first reaching Makkah.

source.text: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Hajj; Sahih Muslim, Book of Hajj

answers.explanation: Walking briskly in the first three circuits of the first tawaf (for men).
Uncovering the right shoulder during the first tawaf (for men).

questions.prompt: Name a name the Qur'an gives to the Day of Judgement.

notAccepted.message: That's the Hereafter in general — name the Day itself. Try again!

answers.explanation: The Day of Resurrection; Surah al-Qiyamah opens with an oath by it.
The Day of Recompense, named in al-Fatihah: "Master of the Day of Judgement."
The Hour, whose time only Allah knows.
The Striking Calamity — the title of Surah 101.
The Inevitable Reality — the title of Surah 69.
The Inevitable Event — the title of Surah 56.
The Overwhelming Event — the title of Surah 88.
The Day of Reckoning.
The Day of Sorting, when truth and falsehood are separated.
The Day of Raising the dead.
The Great Overwhelming Catastrophe.
The Deafening Blast.
The Approaching Day, which has drawn near.
The Day of Mutual Loss and Gain — the title of Surah 64.
The Day of Gathering, when all people are assembled.
The Day of Eternity, when the people of Paradise enter it forever.
The Day of Coming Out, when the dead come forth from their graves.
The Day of Meeting.
The Day of Calling Out to one another.
The Day of Regret.
The Day of the promised Warning, when the Trumpet is blown.

questions.prompt: Name a phrase of dhikr — words said in remembrance of Allah.

notAccepted.message: That's a greeting rather than dhikr. Try again!

answers.explanation: "Glory be to Allah" — one of the four words most beloved to Allah.
"All praise is for Allah" — the opening words of al-Fatihah.
"Allah is the Greatest" — the takbir.
"There is no god but Allah" — called the best of remembrance.
"I seek Allah's forgiveness" — the Prophet ﷺ said it more than seventy times a day.
"What Allah has willed" — said on seeing something good.
"If Allah wills" — said about anything planned for the future.
"In the name of Allah" — said before eating, starting a task, and opening the Qur'an.

answers.canonical: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
variants: La hawla wala quwwata illa billah
answers.explanation: "There is no power and no strength except with Allah" — a treasure of Paradise.

answers.canonical: Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un
answers.explanation: "We belong to Allah and to Him we return" — said at a loss or hardship.
Sending blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, as Allah and His angels do.
"May Allah reward you with good" — the best way to thank someone.
Seeking refuge in Allah from Shaytan — said before reciting the Qur'an.
"Glory and praise be to Allah" — said a hundred times a day, sins are forgiven.
"Glory be to Allah the Magnificent" — one of two phrases light on the tongue and heavy on the Scales.
"Allah is sufficient for us, and the best Disposer of affairs."

variants: La ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu minaz zalimin
answers.explanation: "There is no god but You, glory be to You; I have been among the wrongdoers" — said by Yunus inside the whale.
"O Ever-Living, O Sustainer" — the Prophet ﷺ called on Allah with it in distress.
"Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter" — a prayer the Prophet ﷺ made often.

Compiler of the Jami' al-Tirmidhi, which grades each hadith's strength.
Compiler of the Sunan al-Nasa'i, one of the six major collections.
Compiler of the Sunan Ibn Majah, one of the six major collections.
Imam of Madinah, whose al-Muwatta' is one of the earliest hadith books.
Compiler of the Musnad, holding around 27,000 hadith.
Compiler of Riyad al-Salihin and the famous Forty Hadith.
Compiler of the Sunan al-Darimi.
Compiler of the Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah.
Compiler of the Sahih Ibn Hibban.
Al-Hakim al-Naysaburi, compiler of al-Mustadrak.
Compiler of al-Sunan al-Kubra and many other works.
Baghdad hadith master and compiler of a Sunan.
Compiler of the three Mu'jam collections.
'Abd al-Razzaq al-San'ani, compiler of an early Musannaf.
Compiler of a large early Musannaf.
Hanafi scholar who compiled Sharh Ma'ani al-Athar.
Compiler of Masabih al-Sunnah.
